independent.summary: `honorRobots` is unreachable through the API and is silently reverted: it is absent from FIELD_RULES.crawlSettings, so validateEntityUpdates drops it from any PATCH body (`if (!nestedRule) continue`), and because the validator rebuilds `crawlSettings` as a whole object from only the four declared keys, `Entity.findOneAndUpdate({crawlSettings:{...}})` $sets the entire nested object — so a value Daniel enables directly in the DB is wiped back to false the next time any owner saves Settings.vue (whose form also carries only the four keys).

The Pass 1 structural-analysis fetch of the base URL happens before the crawl loop and bypasses shouldSkipUrl entirely, so with honorRobots on a robots-disallowed home page is still requested (and its DOM sent to Haiku) — breaking the 'never fetched' guarantee the on-flag containment test asserts for non-base URLs; the same bypass exists in rescrapeSite:1003.

summariseRobots iterates the process-wide `hostCache`, not the hosts of the current run, so within the one-hour TTL a run logs per-host 'N URL(s) disallowed' lines for hosts belonging to other entities' crawls, prefixed with this run's domain label (very visible in leoRefresh's sequential per-entity loop); relatedly the 'robots.txt from cache' branch is unreachable because hostCache stores each entry's fetch-time `from`, so a host carried over from an earlier run is reported as freshly 'fetched'.

A full/force scrape deletes all scraped chunks and ScrapedPages before crawling, so with honorRobots on a robots.txt that disallows the base path (or `Disallow: /`) makes the crawl skip the seed URL, discover no links, and leave the entity with an empty knowledge base — recoverable only from the snapshot, and nothing in the gate exempts the entity's own seed URL.

pickGroup resolves groups by substring-matching agent tokens against the whole UA string including its URL (`uaLower.includes(agent)`) rather than the product token, so a group named e.g. `ai`, `chat`, `leo` or `crawler` is treated as LeoAI-specific and overrides the `*` group; and only the first `User-agent: *` group is used, so rules in a second wildcard group (common in plugin-appended robots.txt) are never recorded.

triageGrades.reason: No authentication, permission or role logic is changed; the scrape and dashboard routes keep their existing requireAuth guards.
Only a new non-sensitive ROBOTS_LOG_LEVEL knob is added to .env.example; no credentials, tokens or keys are touched.
Nothing in the diff touches billing, Stripe, quota or pricing paths.

The diff itself adds only additive writes (one snapshot field) and an opt-in, default-off skip; it adds no delete or overwrite of its own, even though it can interact with the pre-existing delete-then-crawl in a full scrape.

Right verdict — the change adds a new outbound HTTP GET of third-party /robots.txt and alters the User-Agent sent to every crawled host — though the cited line 183 is inside matchingRule, not the axios call.
No version bump, build/deploy config or migration is involved; the new Entity and ScrapeSnapshot fields are optional with defaults and the env var falls back to 'light'.
